title: The Gilded Hollow Anew
premise: Freya Eastwick steals memories for coin, bottling other people's pasts in glass vials she sells to the highest bidder. When the border wards of Thornfell collapse on the night the stars vanish, she discovers her own stolen childhood memory holds the last living dragon-fire — and that a cabal of wardens will burn the mountains to reclaim it. Hunted alongside a disgraced warden and a starless child who remembers everything, Freya must choose between selling the secret that could reignite the ancient war or giving up the only proof of who she truly is. In the end, she releases the dragon-fire into the sky, relighting the stars at the cost of her own memories, and finds that the family who remains chooses to remember her.
about_author: Yara Delacroix is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about borders, both drawn on maps and drawn in hearts, from a cabin full of half-finished atlases.

chapters.title: The Vial Seller's Road
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya runs her usual smuggling route through Thornfell, trading bottled memories to desperate nobles while dodging the warden patrols. A routine job goes wrong when a client's vial cracks and she glimpses a memory of dragon-fire — something that shouldn't exist anymore. Emotional beat: restless competence masking a hollow loneliness.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The border wards shatter and every star in the sky goes dark simultaneously; in the chaos, Freya is caught mid-heist by a disgraced warden named Corvin Ashgrave. Instead of arresting her, he begs her help, claiming the wards fell from inside. Emotional beat: fear curdling into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Glass Remembers
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin examines Freya's stolen inventory and realizes one vial contains true dragon-fire — and it belongs to Freya herself, taken from her as a child. He conceals this discovery, torn between duty and growing trust. Emotional beat: guilt over secrets kept for protective reasons.

chapters.title: The Starless Child
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Fleeing warden hunters, they rescue a mute child, Wren, found wandering the pass — a child who can see the extinguished stars and speaks in borrowed voices. Wren recognizes Freya on sight. Emotional beat: unexpected tenderness cracking open Freya's guarded heart.

chapters.title: Warden's Gambit
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. The warden cabal, led by High Warden Serevan, corners the trio in a mountain shrine; Corvin learns Serevan orchestrated the wards' fall to flush out the dragon-fire. Corvin betrays his oaths openly to save Freya and Wren. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty finally paid in full.

chapters.title: Ashes of the First War
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Sheltering in ruins of the ancient war, Wren restores fragments of Freya's stolen childhood: she was a fire-keeper's daughter, her memory harvested to hide the last flame. Freya rages at the theft of her own identity. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into fierce purpose.

chapters.title: The Bargain Below
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. To reach the flame's resting place, the trio descends into the Hollow, where Serevan offers Corvin reinstatement and Freya her memories back — if she surrenders the fire. Tempted by the self she lost, Freya nearly accepts. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive and terrible.

chapters.title: Guttering Light
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The dragon-fire begins to die, and with it any hope of restoring the stars; Wren weakens, bound to the flame's survival. Freya realizes keeping the secret means letting both the child and the sky go dark. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, climax. At the Hollow's heart, Freya confronts Serevan and releases the dragon-fire rather than let it be weaponized; the flame roars skyward and the stars reignite, burning away her stolen vials and every memory she ever kept — including pieces of herself. Emotional beat: triumphant devastation.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV, resolution. Memory-less Freya wakes beneath returned stars, knowing nothing of her past; Corvin and Wren stay beside her, telling her story piece by piece and choosing to build a new one together. Some things, the book closes, are worth being remembered into. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging.
